The database schema for the database rschema_0417 consists of 8 tables. The primary tables are 'user', 'post', 'comment', 'category', 'notification_information', 'comment_reply', and 'comment_post'.
The 'user' table represents the users of the application. It has columns for user_id, user_name, email, password, avatar_link, and registration_date. The user_id is the primary key.
The 'post' table represents the posts made by users. It has columns for post_id, title, content, category_belonging, posting_user, posting_time, status, reply_count, like_count, and favorite_count. The post_id is the primary key and the posting_user and category_belonging are foreign keys referencing the user and category tables respectively.
The 'comment' table represents the comments made by users on posts. It has columns for comment_id, comment_content, posting_user, like_count, reply_count, and posting_time. The comment_id is the primary key and the posting_user is a foreign key referencing the user table.
The 'category' table represents the categories of posts. It has columns for category_id and category_name. The category_id is the primary key.
The 'notification_information' table represents the notifications. It has columns for message_number and notification_content. The message_number is the primary key.
The 'comment_reply' table represents the replies to comments. It has columns for comment_id and reply_comment_id. The comment_id and reply_comment_id are foreign keys referencing the comment table.
The 'comment_post' table represents the relationship between comments and posts. It has columns for comment_id and post_id. The comment_id and post_id are foreign keys referencing the comment and post tables respectively.
The 'notification_distribution' table represents the distribution of notifications to users. It has columns for notification_message_number, user_id, and read_status. The user_id and notification_message_number are foreign keys referencing the user and notification_information tables respectively. The read_status column indicates whether the notification has been read by the user.
All columns allow null values except for the ones that are marked NOT NULL. Default values are not specified for any columns. The database engine is InnoDB and the default character set is utf8mb3.
gold_question: Business requirement description for the forum management system: The forum management system is used to manage users, posts, comments, categories, and notification information. The system contains multiple users, each user has a user ID, username, email, password, avatar link, and registration date. The system records multiple posts, each post has a post ID, title, content, category, posting user, posting time, status, reply count, like count, and favorite count, where the posting user is associated with the user ID of the user, and the category is associated with the category ID of the category. The system also records multiple comments, each comment has a comment ID, comment content, posting user, like count, reply count, and posting time, where the posting user is associated with the user ID of the user. The system supports nested replies for comments, each comment can reply to other comments or posts. The system also contains multiple categories, each category has a category ID and category name, used for categorizing and managing posts. The system records notification information, each notification has a message number and notification content, and is associated with the user, recording the user's read status. The system realizes comprehensive management of various forum information through user table, post table, comment table, category table, and notification information table, ensuring data integrity and traceability.

-- Schema for database: rschema_0417
CREATE TABLE `user` (
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `user_name` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `email` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `password` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `avatar_link` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `registration_date` datetime DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`user_id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `post` (
  `post_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `title` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `content` text DEFAULT NULL,
  `category_belonging` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  `posting_user` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  `posting_time` datetime DEFAULT NULL,
  `status` varchar(50) DEFAULT NULL,
  `reply_count` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  `like_count` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  `favorite_count` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`post_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `post_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`posting_user`) REFERENCES `user` (`user_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `post_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`category_belonging`) REFERENCES `category` (`category_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `comment` (
  `comment_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `comment_content` text DEFAULT NULL,
  `posting_user` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  `like_count` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  `reply_count` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  `posting_time` datetime DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`comment_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `comment_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`posting_user`) REFERENCES `user` (`user_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `category` (
  `category_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `category_name` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`category_id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `notification_information` (
  `message_number` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `notification_content` text DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`message_number`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `comment_reply` (
  `comment_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `reply_comment_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`comment_id`, `reply_comment_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `comment_reply_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`comment_id`) REFERENCES `comment` (`comment_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `comment_reply_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`reply_comment_id`) REFERENCES `comment` (`comment_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `comment_post` (
  `comment_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `post_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`comment_id`, `post_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `comment_post_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`comment_id`) REFERENCES `comment` (`comment_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `comment_post_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`post_id`) REFERENCES `post` (`post_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `notification_distribution` (
  `notification_message_number` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `read_status` tinyint(1) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`notification_message_number`, `user_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `notification_distribution_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`notification_message_number`) REFERENCES `notification_information` (`message_number`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `notification_distribution_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id`) REFERENCES `user` (`user_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;
